scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Your screen dims in a dark room, and switches off when you hold the phone to your ear. How does it know?

scenes.name: light
scenes.text: Near the top of the screen is an ambient light sensor. It measures how bright the room around you is.

scenes.name: adjust
scenes.text: Bright room, brighter screen. Dark room, dimmer screen. That saves battery, and is easier on your eyes.

scenes.name: learn
scenes.text: Many phones also learn from you. Each time you nudge the slider, adaptive brightness adjusts to your taste.

scenes.name: prox
scenes.text: The proximity sensor sends out invisible infrared light. When something is close, like your ear, the light bounces straight back.

scenes.name: off
scenes.text: So during a call, the phone turns the screen off, and your cheek can't accidentally tap buttons. It also saves power.

scenes.name: hidden
scenes.text: On many new phones, these sensors hide under the screen itself, so you won't even see them.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Light, brightness, infrared, ear. Little sensors, big help. Follow for more on how things really work.
